To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there is a great deal of variation in clinical ethics consultation practice, that this variation is largely a function of variation in the institutional setting of clinical ethics consultation, and that the variation in consultation practice is a function of variation both in the nature of the clinical setting and in the nature of clinical ethics itself.

clinical ethicists do a variety of things in a variety of settings, and that the kind of ethics that is most helpful in these settings is a kind of “practical” ethics that is not very theoretical, and that is not much like the kind of ethics taught in philosophy departments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: What is clinical ethics?
the following questions: What are the different paradigms of clinical ethics consultation?
the question of whether there is a single “clinical ethics consultation paradigm” and, if not, what are the different paradigms?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical ethicist is a person who has a professional interest in and a commitment to the practice of bioethics in a clinical setting.
clinical ethics consultants do not have a common practice.
there is no one right answer to these questions, and no one paradigm that can be applied to all clinical settings and situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is “clinical ethics” in the sense that it is applied ethics, but it is not clinical in the sense that we are clinicians.
we provide clinical ethics consultation services.

we are engaged in the process of helping patients, their families, health care professionals, and others in the health care system to understand, assess, and resolve ethical problems arising in the course of health care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a lot of variety in the way clinical ethics consultation is conducted.

the practice of clinical ethics consultation is not a unitary phenomenon, and that there is a need for more research into the different kinds of clinical ethics consultation practice that are in use in different settings.
there is no single “right way” to be an ethics consultant.
